source.title: Scaling cross-tissue single-cell annotation models
source.authors: Felix Fischer; David S. Fischer; Evan Biederstedt; Alexandra-Chloé Villani; F. Theis

record.file_problem: none; the full article is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling experiments to supervised single-cell transcriptomics classification and reports held-out cross-entropy trends with training-data size; it does not study language models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling experiments for scTab with dataset size and model size. Cross-entropy loss is shown for the dataset-size sweep, but the article does not fit or report a power-law form or exponents. Macro F1 results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version because the claim versions concern language-model loss or downstream performance.
record.test_reason: Weak T3 test of V5. The study varies training-data size for a supervised single-cell transcriptomics classifier (scTab) and reports held-out cross-entropy loss in Fig. 2b. It never fits a power law or reports exponents, so it bears on V5 only as whether loss scales with data at all, and on what the data axis should count.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: classification performance scales with training data size and model size, and data scaling is dominated by batch/donor diversity rather than cell count. The authors also stress that nonlinear models are needed to benefit from scale.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains supervised single-cell classifiers, measures classification loss and macro F1, and varies donor/cell data size or parameter count. It does not reproduce language-model pretraining scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed dataset-size scaling differs between donor-based subsampling and random cell-based subsampling.

fits_no_version.finding: Macro F1 scales strongly with donor-based data size and weakly with cell-based size. A linear baseline's learning curve flattens earlier (Fig. 2d).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In single-cell classification, performance gains from more data are driven by donor/batch diversity and require nonlinear models.

fits_no_version.finding: Macro F1 rises from 0.7864 (1.7M parameters) to 0.8323 (16.2M parameters) on the full data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger scTab models classify better over the tested parameter range.

record.problems: The cross-entropy scaling values are presented only in a figure, and no power-law fits or exponents are reported. The authors also note that annotation inconsistencies across datasets are a confounding factor.
record.rows_left_out: No additional language-model loss, compute-optimal allocation, or power-law-fit results are reported. Other classification comparisons and data-augmentation results do not measure a claim version's named language-model loss behavior.

untested.parts: Power-law form and exponents; loss scaling with model size; extrapolation; image, video, repeated-data and fine-tuning regimes.
Not tested: no language-model downstream tasks.

missing.what: Whether Fig. 2f (model-size sweep) also plots cross-entropy loss. The caption is ambiguous; if it does, that would be a V5 model-size loss row.

record.verdict_notes: Kaplan et al. is cited only as motivation. Loss trends are figure-only with no power-law fit, so support for V5's functional form cannot be assessed. The single limits_scope verdict rests on the authors' explicit text contrast between donor-based and cell-based subsampling.

versions.untested_parts: No language models or held-out language-model pretraining loss; no power-law fit against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from small language-model runs to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation experiment or compute-optimal parameter/token split.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.

The study tests dataset-size-related cross-entropy trends in single-cell classification, but does not test whether they follow a power law or fit exponents. It does not test model-size loss scaling, other modalities beyond single-cell transcriptomics, or the other listed training regimes.
No downstream-task performance scaling for language models or relationship between language-model pretraining loss and downstream performance.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, or tests of power-law curve bending or fitting-method dependence.

relationships.condition: scTab single-cell classification, data-size sweep: donor-based vs random cell-based subsampling
relationships.reason: Held-out loss falls strongly as donors are added but much more weakly as cells are added (r1, r2). Data scaling depends on diversity, not raw example count. No power-law form is shown.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out loss decreased strongly when donors were added but much less when cells were added, without an established power-law form.
